intro: Ko Pha Ngan's great tree is a Yang Na in the village of Ban Nok, in the south of the island, a few kilometres from the Thong Sala pier. Thailand's Ministry of Culture listed it as a heritage tree of the land in 2018 and recorded a girth of 14.64 metres, a height of 53.5 metres and an age of about 400 years. It stands beside the public road, free to see, with small spirit houses at its foot.
meta_description: Ko Pha Ngan's giant Yang Na in Ban Nok: about 400 years old and 53.5 metres tall by Thailand's heritage tree register, free beside the road.
question_meta: The oldest tree on Ko Pha Ngan is the giant Yang Na of Ban Nok, about 400 years old by Thailand's heritage tree register.
question_answer: The oldest tree we know of on Ko Pha Ngan is the giant Yang Na in Ban Nok, in the south of the island. Thailand's Ministry of Culture put it at about 400 years when it listed the tree as a heritage tree of the land in 2018. The age is an estimate, not a count of rings.
question_context: The tree is a Yang Na, Dipterocarpus alatus, a tall tropical tree of the dipterocarp family. The Ministry of Culture's 2018 list of heritage trees of the land records a girth of 14.64 metres and a height of 53.5 metres, and says the tree won first prize in a 1999 Kasetsart University contest for the largest Yang Na. The register calls it the biggest Yang Na in Thailand; we have not found an independent national survey to confirm that. Other Yang Na grow around the village, and the register notes that bees nest in this one's crown. The tree stands beside the public road in Ban Nok, about 300 metres past Wat Pho in the Ban Tai area, roughly four to five kilometres from Thong Sala pier, where the ferries from Ko Samui and Surat Thani come in. It is free to see at any hour. Villagers treat it as sacred, so the spirit houses and cloth at its foot are offerings, and the low fence keeps the ground around it clear.

faq.q: Is the giant tree on Ko Pha Ngan free to visit?
faq.a: Yes. It stands beside the public road in Ban Nok, about 300 metres past Wat Pho, with no gate or fee. The road is narrow, so daylight is the better time.

faq.q: How big is the Yang Na of Ban Nok?
faq.a: Thailand's heritage tree register records a girth of 14.64 metres and a height of 53.5 metres. The girth may include the swelling at the base.

faq.q: How do I get there from Thong Sala?
faq.a: It is about four to five kilometres from Thong Sala pier, by songthaew towards Ban Tai, taxi or hired motorbike. We have not checked times or fares.

trees.story:
On a narrow road through Ban Nok, a village in the south of Ko Pha Ngan, one Yang Na rises as a pale grey column past the power lines and only starts to branch far above the rooftops.

Thailand's Ministry of Culture listed it in 2018 as a heritage tree of the land and recorded a girth of 14.64 metres, a height of 53.5 metres and an age of about 400 years. The age is an estimate, so read it as a rough figure. The register adds that the tree won first prize in a 1999 Kasetsart University contest for the largest Yang Na and calls it the biggest in Thailand. That is the register's claim, and we have not found a national survey to check it against.

Yang Na is a tall tropical tree of the dipterocarp family, and more of them grow around the village. The register notes that bees nest in this one's crown. Ban Nok treats the tree as sacred, with small spirit houses at its foot, coloured cloth wound round the trunk and a low wooden fence keeping the ground clear.

It stands beside the public road about 300 metres past Wat Pho, a few kilometres from the Thong Sala pier, and is free to see at any hour. Come in daylight, because the road is narrow. If you go, tell us how it looks now.

trees.access: Free, beside the public road, open at all hours; daytime advised. Narrow road, busy about 11:00 to 14:00. Few facilities. Villagers treat it as sacred; small shrines at the foot.
trees.transport: About 4 to 5 km from Thong Sala pier; Thong Sala to Ban Tai/Ban Khai songthaew, or taxi or hired motorbike (lovethailand, travellingfoot). Not checked on site.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its pale grey trunk, bare for most of its height, rising from a fenced plot beside the road with small spirit houses and coloured cloth at its foot, about 300 metres past Wat Pho in Ban Nok.
trees.verify_notes: Register: 400 years, girth 14.64 m, height 53.5 m (girth measured by the register, presumably at breast height; may include buttress swell, unverified). Register history says it won first prize in a Kasetsart University contest for the largest Yang Na (17 Nov 1999) and is called the biggest Yang Na in Thailand: a register/sign claim, not independently verified; do not repeat as fact without attribution. Many more Yang Na stand in the same area, this being the 'mother tree'. Bees nest in the crown. Cared for by the Ban Nok community (Moo 2). PIN: the register coordinate 9.7009,100.0225 is about 800 m off; lovethailand's navigation link (9.70544,100.02893) and thailandee's GPS (9.705272,100.028882) agree within 20 m and match the textual 'about 300 m past Wat Pho'. Another lovethailand point (9.717583,100.034081) is the page's 'check-in' point, 1.4 km north, ignored. Published tourist-guide GPS, not our own fix. 53.5 m is tall for Yang Na but within the species range (up to about 50 m+) and repeated by Lonely Planet (54 m). ALIVE: Lonely Planet (2026-branded page) and lovethailand (recently updated) both list it as visitable; no dated first-hand 2025 report found; flagged.
